description: DARTS: Multi-year database of AI-detected retrogressive thaw slumps in the circum-arctic permafrost region is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Ingmar Nitze et al. Retrogressive Thaw Slumps (RTS) are widespread mass-wasting hillslope failures triggered by thawing permafrost. While regional studies have provided insights into the spatial distribution and dynamics of RTS, a consistent and unbiased quantification and monitoring remains unsolved at pan-arctic scales. Coverage: not stated; published in 2025. Formats: XML, GeoPackage, Parquet, Image, Python. The data are held in NSF Arctic Data Center and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence of the data is not stated in the sources read (the paper itself is open access). Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked, and the coverage and resolution are those of the abstract only. It can support transport-network, traffic and mobility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
